name: Selegiline
lead: Selegiline, also called deprenyl, is a selective, irreversible inhibitor of monoamine oxidase B (MAO-B), an enzyme that breaks down dopamine. It is prescribed mainly as an add-on for Parkinson's disease, and a transdermal patch form is approved for depression [1].

In looksmaxxing and nootropic circles it is discussed as a dopamine-supporting, recovery and longevity compound: proponents link it to better mood, drive, focus and healthy aging, which they connect to training consistency and a more youthful presentation. These are claims from communities; the research base is in medical conditions rather than appearance [3].

The US label describes it as an adjunct to levodopa/carbidopa in Parkinson's patients whose response has deteriorated [4]. A 2022 review of cognitive enhancers lists selegiline among drugs used by healthy people, noting that effects in healthy individuals are uncertain and reported improvements temporary [3].

angle.text: Selegiline is used by some people to support dopamine, mood and focus, which they say helps them stay consistent with training and self-care. Any link to appearance is through this indirect chain [3].

infobox: Oral tablet or capsule; transdermal patch

paras: The US label indicates selegiline tablets as an adjunct in Parkinson's patients on levodopa/carbidopa who show a deteriorating response; the label notes no controlled-study evidence of benefit without levodopa [4]. The transdermal form, Emsam, is approved for major depressive disorder [1]. Parkinson's treatment reviews cover its place among motor-symptom therapies [9].

sections.h: Use in looksmaxxing and nootropic communities
paras: Selegiline is discussed as a cognitive enhancer and as an anti-aging agent. A review of smart drugs in healthy individuals includes it, describing users' enthusiastic anecdotal reports alongside uncertain efficacy in non-impaired brains [3].

At doses used for Parkinson's disease, selegiline selectively inhibits MAO-B, which raises dopamine in the brain; at higher doses selectivity falls and MAO-A is also inhibited [1]. The label warns that selectivity may not be absolute and that hypertensive reactions with tyramine-rich foods have been reported rarely at recommended doses [4].

The label cautions against exceeding recommended daily doses because of non-selective MAO inhibition risks [4]. Drug interactions are a major consideration for MAO inhibitors, and the label lists pregnancy category C [4].

Grokipedia attributes its development to Hungarian pharmacologist Jozsef Knoll in the 1960s, with US approval for Parkinson's in 1989 and the patch for depression in 2006 [1]. A 1989 Science paper examined deprenyl's effect on the natural history of Parkinson's [8].

Studies include a 1997 randomized trial of selegiline and vitamin E in 341 patients with moderately severe Alzheimer's disease [5], a 1984 open trial in 17 patients with atypical depression, 10 of whom responded [6], a trial in narcolepsy [10], and registered trials in Parkinson's daytime sleepiness [11], cocaine dependence [12], smoking cessation [13] and others. A review of cognitive enhancers found efficacy in healthy people uncertain [3]. No studies found for cosmetic or appearance outcomes.

lore.intro: Selegiline is discussed in nootropic and anti-aging corners of enthusiast communities as a dopamine-supporting compound; it is less central to looksmaxxing forums than to biohacking.

claims.claim: It boosts motivation, focus and mood in healthy people.
claims.believers: Users describe sharper drive and mood, which they tie to consistent training.
claims.experts: A 2022 review says efficacy in healthy individuals is uncertain and any improvement temporary [3].

claims.claim: It slows aging and extends lifespan.
claims.believers: Proponents cite early animal-lifespan work and neuroprotection claims.
claims.experts: Trials in Parkinson's and Alzheimer's have examined disease progression [5][8]; no study has tested aging appearance.

card.summary: A prescription MAO-B inhibitor that raises brain dopamine; some people use it for mood, drive and recovery, and it is also discussed as a nootropic.
card.note: Prescription drug; MAO inhibition carries serious drug and food interaction cautions.

quick.overview:
Selegiline is a prescription drug that blocks the MAO-B enzyme, letting dopamine last longer in the brain. It is used for Parkinson's disease, and a patch form for depression.

Some people in nootropic and biohacking communities use it hoping for better mood, focus and drive, which they link to training and self-care.
quick.mechanism: It irreversibly inhibits MAO-B, reducing dopamine breakdown; at higher doses it also inhibits MAO-A [1].
quick.risks: Labelling warns about exceeding recommended doses and about interactions, including rare hypertensive reactions with tyramine-rich foods [4]. It is prescription-only.
